metadata.title: A Standing Wave Is Two Waves That Never Stop Moving
metadata.register: formal, undergrad/grad audience, no casual narration
metadata.branding: none — unbranded, book content only, no channel/logo/handle

beats.narration_text: Two identical waves travel in opposite directions. What happens when they meet?
beats.new_visual_element: Portrait-only opening question card (title-styled, crimson underline).

beats.narration_text: Consider two identical waves on the same string, with the same amplitude, the same wavelength, and the same frequency. One travels to the right, and the other travels to the left. What happens when they meet?
beats.new_visual_element: Two stacked horizontal axes sharing one x-scale. Top: a teal sinusoid traveling continuously to the right, labeled with a rightward arrow. Bottom: a crimson sinusoid of identical amplitude and wavelength traveling continuously to the left, labeled with a leftward arrow.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: two separate traveling waves, opposite directions, same scale

beats.narration_text: The principle of superposition answers the question. At every point, and at every instant, the displacement of the string is the sum of the two individual displacements. Adding the two waves point by point gives a single resultant wave.
beats.new_visual_element: Both component waves slide onto one shared axis and dim to about thirty percent opacity, still traveling. A thick black curve, recomputed every frame as the literal point-by-point sum of the two, grows in on top.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: one axis: faint teal (right-moving) and faint crimson (left-moving) components, bold black sum curve

beats.narration_text: Certain points on the string never move at all. At every multiple of half a wavelength, the two waves always cancel exactly, so the displacement there is zero for all time. These fixed points are called nodes.
beats.new_visual_element: Slate dots appear on the axis at every multiple of half a wavelength, each with a thin dashed vertical guideline. The black sum curve keeps passing through every dot, frame after frame. One dot is labeled node.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: faint components, black sum curve, node dots with dashed guides, one node label

beats.narration_text: Halfway between neighboring nodes, at odd multiples of a quarter wavelength, the two waves reinforce. There the string swings through its largest displacement, twice the amplitude of either wave alone. These points are called antinodes.
beats.new_visual_element: Gold bands centered on each antinode, whose height tracks the sum curve's instantaneous envelope, two A times the absolute value of cosine omega t, so they pulse in sync with the motion. One band is labeled antinode.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: faint components, black sum curve, node dots, pulsing gold antinode bands, node and antinode labels

beats.narration_text: The algebra makes this exact. The sum of the two traveling waves is two A sine k x, times cosine omega t. A fixed shape in space, multiplied by an oscillation in time. The pattern stays in place, even though both waves underneath are still traveling.
beats.new_visual_element: The equation y(x,t) = [2A sin(kx)] cos(omega t) above the axis, with the spatial factor in black and the temporal factor in teal. The faint components keep sliding beneath the stationary pattern.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: equation, faint moving components, black sum curve, nodes, pulsing antinode bands

beats.narration_text: A standing wave is not a wave that has stopped moving. It is two waves moving in opposite directions, canceling at fixed points and reinforcing between them. Energy no longer travels along the string. It oscillates in place, between the nodes.
beats.new_visual_element: Summary line locks in: STANDING WAVE = TWO TRAVELING WAVES, OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. Everything else keeps moving: faint components sliding, sum curve oscillating, antinode bands pulsing.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: final held frame: summary, equation, faint components, sum curve, nodes, antinode bands
